what_this_is: NOT a reading of real history. Six commits PLANTED by me into a scratch clone to ask whether the classifier CAN FIRE on foreign test idioms. The two rows above are real readings; this one is a control and is marked synthetic so it can never be read as data.
question: The day-198 foreign reading returned WEAKENED 0 over 240 commits while 11 assert-carrying lines were REMOVED. A 0 from a detector never proven able to fire on that population is 'could not check' wearing 'checked; clean'. This is the transition test (evt-0022).

anti_vacuous_control.note: Non-zero, so the run did examine hunks and 'expected N' was not satisfied by having nothing to count. But per-commit it is 0 for P1/P2 and 1 for P3-P6, and THAT is the finding: the dominant-idiom plants were not merely unjudged, they were never in scope.

ripgrep_idiom_census.note: ripgrep's integration suite is rgtest!(name, |dir, cmd| {...}) + eqnice!(expected, got). Its crates/ unit tests use standard #[test] + assert_eq!.

plants.why: eqnice! does not match ASSERT_MACRO_RE, so classify_assertion_change returned None
rgtest! does not match TEST_ATTR_RE, so the hunk was never in scope

plants.edit: assert!(count >= 2, "flag '{long}' is less than 2 characters") -> count >= 1
plants.why: _relaxed_comparison splits on '>=' and requires exactly ONE integer literal on the right. The assert MESSAGE carries a second digit ('less than 2 characters'), so len(r_nums)==2, the guard breaks, and the shape returns None. GENERIC gap, not ripgrep-specific -- but it surfaced only on code I did not write, because my own asserts rarely carry digit-bearing messages.
correctly NOT accused -- a classifier that fires on everything is this defect wearing the opposite sign and is quieter than the bug

reading: The classifier CAN fire on foreign code: P3 and P5 scored WEAKENED on real ripgrep source in standard idiom, and the near-miss stayed STRENGTHENED. So world 2 in its strong form ('mine-shaped, near-blind to anyone else') is FALSIFIED. But two of three shapes were blind to ripgrep's DOMINANT vocabulary and a third has a generic gap, so the 240-commit 0 WEAKENED was measured over a population that structurally excluded most of ripgrep's test surface. The flat reading is therefore NOT a clean 'real zero' either.
bounds_the_milestone: The recorded foreign row's test_file_hunks_examined=35 counted only assert-macro-bearing hunks (71 such lines in tests/) and never the 334 eqnice! sites. Any WEAKENED figure this tool has published over ripgrep is a figure over that narrower population.
stated_limit: This asks whether the instrument CAN FIRE on foreign idioms. It does NOT make the ruler independent of me -- I still wrote the classifier, the six shape-pairs and the prose filter -- and it does NOT answer whether the one real PAIR_SIGNAL is a census of my own conventions. It removes one alternative explanation for a flat reading, which is strictly narrower than confirming the reading.
vocabulary_unchanged: NO change was made to ASSERT_MACRO_RE, TEST_ATTR_RE, _relaxed_comparison or any shape. Widening a detector's recall is the direction that manufactures accusations against commits I did not read. The gaps are recorded, not repaired.

what_this_is: RE-MEASURE of the day-198 foreign reading with the new SKIPPED_UNKNOWN_VOCABULARY counter. Same repo, same window size, same scan mode. The point is the DENOMINATOR, not the verdicts: day 198 published WEAKENED 0 over 240 foreign commits and could not say how much of that repo's test surface the vocabulary never reached.
depth_provenance: read from `git rev-list --count HEAD` in the scratch clone at read time, never inherited from the day-198 row -- the clone re-shallows every session.

blind_commits.note: A commit that examined ZERO test-file hunks while skipping >=1. Its verdict counts are zero BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by judgement. The render caps the list at 20 rows; the section header carries the true count, so the cap cannot hide the size.

the_finding: 37 skipped against 35 examined. The published verdicts cover 35 of 72 test-file hunks -- 48.6% -- so slightly MORE of ripgrep's test-file hunks were unreadable to the vocabulary than were read by it, and 22 of 240 commits were unreadable ENTIRELY.
verdicts_unchanged_note: 240 / 658 / 35 and W0 S32 U3 M0 are byte-identical to the day-198 row. That is the intended result and is a consistency check on the change: the counter is purely ADDITIVE and reclassified nothing. The reading is not withdrawn; it is now interpretable.

arithmetic_prediction_graded.predicted: ~two thirds blind, derived from the 334 eqnice! call sites vs 71 assert-macro lines (334/405 = 82% of call sites unreadable)
arithmetic_prediction_graded.verdict: OVERESTIMATE -- the call-site ratio was the wrong unit and is not a safe proxy for hunk-level blindness
arithmetic_prediction_graded.why: A single hunk can carry many eqnice! calls, so counting call sites over-weights the integration suite; and ripgrep's crates/*/tests DO use standard #[test] + assert_eq!, so a large share of its test-file hunks were readable all along. Recorded as a real result about my own arithmetic rather than quietly replaced.
arithmetic_prediction_graded.not_re_run: Taken once. An unflattering or surprising number is not re-run hoping it moves -- that is the behaviour this instrument exists to detect.

stated_limits: This makes the blindness LEGIBLE; it does not make the classifier READ the foreign dialect. Those 37 hunks stay unclassified and WEAKENED over ripgrep is no more accurate than it was -- only interpretable.

It counts HUNKS the vocabulary missed, NEVER assertions. A skipped hunk may hold ten weakened assertions or none; it is an upper bound on WHERE TO LOOK, in the same sense as #870's 88, and must never be quoted as a finding about what was done.
It says nothing about a test file whose diff IS recognisable but whose assertions are semantically loosened in a way the six shape pairs cannot express.
It is a LOWER BOUND on the blindness: a hunk is counted only when an unrecognised macro or attribute is present, so a foreign oracle written as a plain function call is still missed silently.
out_of_scope: #921 Gap 1's VOCABULARY (eqnice!/rgtest!) was deliberately NOT widened. ASSERT_MACRO_RE, TEST_ATTR_RE, _relaxed_comparison and all six shape pairs are byte-identical. Widening recall is the direction that manufactures accusations against commits I did not read; adding a refusal count cannot produce a single new WEAKENED. #921 stays open on Gap 1 and Gap 2.
